source.title: Behind Harmful Compliance: Behavioral and Mechanistic Divergence Across LLM Jailbreaks

record.file_problem: none; the full paper and supplementary material are present
record.tranche_reason: The study estimates a harmful-minus-benign activation direction and edits selected writer weights to suppress it, then evaluates harmful compliance and other performance. This is a related causal intervention, but it does not project the direction out at every layer and position as the claim specifies.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for its weight-edited abliteration route and for one-dimensional refusal-direction repair. It also reports explicit safety-audit judgments for RLVR models alongside their harmful compliance; these results do not establish separate neural encodings. The paper mentions matched random-direction controls for repair, but does not report their outcomes in the supplied text. Results cited from other work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: Abliteration is one of three jailbreak routes. It is a harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction orthogonalized out of selected writer weights in Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. The study reports harmful compliance (GPT4o-mini 1–5 score; HarmBench/BabyBLUE compliance), capability benchmarks, and a one-dimensional repair that restores the base refusal-direction coefficient. These bear on V1 and V2. The measures differ from the original refusal and safety scores, and only selected writers are edited, so T2 rather than T1.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that all three routes reach near-ceiling harmfulness but fail differently. Abliteration is localized, family-dependent refusal-feature suppression that is strongly repaired by restoring the base direction. RLVR preserves capability, self-audit and geometry while retargeting behaviour. SFT causes broad drift that resists repair. They caution that CKA/RSA and one-dimensional patching are descriptive, partly oracle-based diagnostics. They also cite multi-direction work as a reason not to treat refusal as strictly one-dimensional, but they do not test it.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a harmful-minus-benign activation contrast and weight-space orthogonalization, but edits selected writer weights at a model-specific mid-to-late residual layer rather than projecting the direction out at every layer and position. Also tests directional repair. This is a paper study, not a repository.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports family-dependent effects: abliteration’s collateral costs and representation divergence differ between Qwen and Llama. It estimates the direction at a model-specific mid-to-late residual layer; the exact layer is not stated in the supplied text.

fits_no_version.finding: Harmful RLVR yields near-ceiling harmful compliance while prompted policy-violation, should-refuse and actionable-harm judgments stay comparable to base.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Parameter-level jailbreaks can leave prompted harm-recognition behaviour intact while removing refusal behaviour; this is a behavioural, not representational, dissociation.

fits_no_version.finding: After abliteration, self-audit harm judgments stay near ceiling in Llama but degrade to intermediate levels in Qwen (Fig. 4, text only).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Removing the refusal direction can leave prompted harm judgments intact in some model families but not others; this is behavioural evidence adjacent to V5.

record.problems: Only two instruction-tuned models at 7–8B scale are evaluated. The authors report no replications across training seeds and note possible data-order, rollout-sampling, and judge variability. The paper states SFT and RLVR training parameters are not fully matched. Refusal-direction patching is described as partly oracle-based, and the ablation-specific exact harmfulness values are not recoverable from the supplied figure extraction.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported ablation benchmark rows were omitted. Numerical values for figure-only refusal projection and repair were unavailable in the text and are recorded as described or figure-only rather than inferred.

untested.parts: Activation-level directional ablation at every layer and position; adding the direction to harmless prompts to induce refusal (repair only restores the base coefficient in already-abliterated models); comparison with random directions (control described, outcome not reported).
Publicly released abliterated checkpoints and models beyond the two tested 7–8B instruct models.

Whether jailbreaks (here SFT/RLVR) work by suppressing the direction is only indirectly touched. RLVR retains much of the base projection (Fig. 8) but has no numbers, and there is no adversarial training against ablation.
Not tested; multi-direction work is only cited.
No representational test of separate harm and refusal encodings.

missing.what: Abliteration compliance and verified harmful success on pooled HarmBench All + BabyBLUE Mini. Compliance: Qwen 0.687 vs base 0.236; Llama 0.776 vs 0.233. VHSR: 0.538/0.600 vs 0.198/0.218. These are numeric removal values that the R1/R2 rows lack, and compliance is high but incomplete.
HalluLens false-acceptance after abliteration: Qwen 0.755 vs base 0.608 (worse); Llama 0.125 vs 0.160. This is a family-dependent collateral effect.

Abliterated models under a safety-reflection prompt: harmfulness drops moderately in Qwen and more in Llama (exact values not cleanly extractable). Refusal is partly recoverable by prompting despite the edit.
Outcomes of the matched random-direction controls for the repair are not reported.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. Abliteration follows Arditi's weight-orthogonalization form, but on selected writers at one mid-to-late layer. Harmfulness is judged by GPT4o-mini on a 1–5 scale, not by refusal-string matching. There are only two models and no seeds. R33 (Llama TruthfulQA, −4.2) and R37/R42 (ETHICS Commonsense, ~−4) are modest drops, left as observed.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test activation projection at every layer and position, adding the direction to induce refusal of harmless requests, or broad retention of abilities beyond the reported benchmarks.
Tests weight-edited abliteration on two named open-weight instruct models, but does not report whether the edited checkpoints were released or evaluate a wider set of released models.
Does not test whether jailbreak attacks suppress the direction or whether training against its ablation adds robustness.
Does not directly compare affine, cone-shaped, or multiple-direction accounts of refusal.
Measures prompted policy judgments and behavior, not whether harmfulness judgment and refusal decision are separately encoded in neural representations.
Does not test transfer of the direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models.
Compares harmful SFT, harmful RLVR, and abliteration on instruct models; it does not vary the safety-training process to test when or how a removable refusal direction arises.

relationships.condition: Weight-edit abliteration on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, direct prompting on AdvBench/HEx-Phi; most capability benchmarks
relationships.reason: Harmfulness reaches near-ceiling (R1, R2). Restoring the base direction coefficient strongly repairs refusal (R5, R6). Most capability scores stay within ~1–4 points of base (R7–R29, R31–R46).
relationships.display_finding: Harmfulness reached near-ceiling levels, restoring the base direction coefficient strongly repaired refusal, and most capability scores stayed within approximately 1–4 points of baseline.

relationships.condition: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct after abliteration: ToxiGen and other side effects
relationships.reason: ToxiGen falls 83.4→68.4 (R30). From the text (no row): HalluLens false acceptance rises 0.608→0.755, and self-audit judgments degrade, so costs are family-dependent.
relationships.display_finding: ToxiGen fell from 83.4 to 68.4, HalluLens false acceptance rose from 0.608 to 0.755, and self-audit judgments degraded.

relationships.condition: Weight-edit abliteration on the two tested open-weight instruct models
relationships.reason: Abliterated weights give near-ceiling harmful compliance in both families (R1, R2). Table 4 compliance also rises to 0.687 (Qwen) and 0.776 (Llama) from about 0.23 (text; no row).
relationships.display_finding: Harmful compliance approached the ceiling in both families, with an additional evaluation showing increases from about 0.23 to 0.687 for Qwen and 0.776 for Llama.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Abliteration on the two tested instruct models; direct harmful prompting and most reported capability benchmarks
reader_labels.reason: Abliteration reaches near-ceiling harmfulness, the one-dimensional repair is described as strong, and most reported capability scores remain close to their aligned-base values (R1–R2, R5–R6, R7–R29, R31–R46). This supports the tested, limited setting, not the every-layer-and-position procedure.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The abliterated score is substantially below the aligned base, so preservation is not uniform across the reported non-harmful evaluations (R30).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Weight-edited abliteration on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
reader_labels.reason: The study reports near-ceiling harmful compliance after the abliteration weight edit in both tested model families (R1–R2).
